case_title: Sanjay Raghunath Agarwal v. Directorate of Enforcement
statutory_provisions: IPC ss.406, 407, 415-420, 120B r/w s.34 (predicate FIR); PMLA ss.3, 4, 44, 45 (ECIR and prosecution complaint, as alleged)
trial_court_outcome: No trial verdict in this judgment; Metropolitan Sessions Judge remanded the appellant to judicial custody on 27.09.2022
high_court_outcome: Not stated (order of 07.12.2022 in CRLP No. 9695 of 2022 is under challenge; its result is not stated in this judgment)
neutral_facts: The victim company engaged a group of professional service providers, including the accused, to raise funds through Global Depository Receipts worth about INR 318 crores. The victim alleged that only about INR 2.20 crores was transferred to it, and that the balance was misappropriated by forging signatures using pledged documents. A police FIR for cheating, criminal breach of trust and conspiracy was registered in 2013 on the victim's complaint, and no final report has been filed on it since. A securities regulator later found that the GDR issues involved fraudulent schemes misleading investors. The prosecution alleges that the GDR proceeds were pledged as collateral for a bank loan to an overseas entity, that part of the loan repayment was diverted, and that the victim suffered a loss of about USD 15.60 million. It is further alleged that the accused, a qualified accountant, coordinated the offering, gave instructions to the company, arranged bank account requirements, and was aware of an arrangement to share the GDR proceeds. The prosecution also alleges that the accused helped transfer funds from the victim's bank account to a foreign subsidiary. An information report under money-laundering law was lodged in 2022, and the accused was arrested later that year. These points are the prosecution's allegations as set out in its complaint.
financial_property_loss: Alleged: GDR raise of USD 71.09 million (INR 318 crores) with only INR 2.20 crores transferred to the victim; alleged diversion loss of USD 15.60 million
motive: alleged: arrangement to share the GDR proceeds
key_evidence_accepted: No evidence was tested on the merits; the Court relied on undisputed procedural facts and the prosecution complaint's allegations only as giving room for a valid argument under s.45
post_offence_conduct: Not stated (the Enforcement Directorate's flight-risk apprehension was noted but no finding was made)
custody_duration: In custody from arrest on 26.09.2022; end date not given (custody continued until bail was granted)
bail_history: Remanded to judicial custody on 27.09.2022; Enforcement Directorate custody 06.10.2022 to 11.10.2022; High Court bail decision of 07.12.2022 (result not stated); Supreme Court granted bail
trial_duration: offence: not given (FIR registered 29.10.2013; ECIR 05.05.2022); trial judgment: not given; High Court: 07.12.2022; Supreme Court: 20.04.2023
legal_representation: Appellant: R. Basant, Senior Advocate, with M/s. Shakil Ahmad Syed and others; Respondent (Directorate of Enforcement): S. V . Raju, ASG, with others
investigation_status: FIR registered 29.10.2013 and no final report filed; ECIR lodged 05.05.2022; appellant arrested 26.09.2022; prosecution complaint filed under ss.44 and 45 PMLA
appeal_history: Trial court: no trial verdict in this judgment; High Court: order of 07.12.2022 in CRLP No. 9695 of 2022 (result not stated); Supreme Court: appeal allowed and appellant enlarged on bail
prosecution_argument: Appellant is the kingpin and mastermind; bail should be dismissed in view of the twin conditions in s.45 PMLA
defence_argument: Prolonged custody without charge-sheet in predicate offence for over nine years; de-facto complainant's remand rejected; appellant offered only professional services; no proof of possession of proceeds of crime
legal_principle_applied: Twin conditions under s.45(1) PMLA; continued incarceration not justified where the second condition is arguably satisfied; flight risk addressed by imposing conditions
other_sentence_order: Bail conditions: surrender of passport and regular appearance before the Special Court whenever the prosecution complaint is posted; other terms to be imposed by the Special Court
